title: What If Coffee Started to Disappear?

scenes.text: What if coffee started to disappear? Scientists say it's already at risk.
Kew researchers checked 124 wild coffee species and found 75 of them, sixty percent, at risk of extinction.
That includes Arabica, the species behind most of the world's coffee, now classed as endangered in the wild.
In Ethiopia, Arabica output could fall by as much as eighty-five percent by 2080.
Robusta, grown more widely, is at least forty percent of the global coffee trade by value.
And about forty-five percent of wild species are missing from seed banks and living collections. The backup plan is thin.
